page.layout: One page of running text in a single main column; catchword "CAPVT" at the lower right of the text block; a narrow strip of show-through from the facing page at the right edge (not transcribed). No marginal notes on this page.

main_text.p: Diuisio partium proprie inuentio est quoti, ad diui-dendum ita se habentis, sicut unitas ad diuisorem. Vnde manifestum euadit, quotum diuisis partibus necessario maiorem esse, contra quàm integrorum diuisio compa-rata est. Inuentio hæc ex diuisione numerorum datis partibus proportionalium, existit, cùm partes ipsæ per se diuidi non possint.

Sint igitur primùm cognominēs hæ partes 9/10 per 3/10 diuidendæ. Hic igitur eas per priorem reductionem ad integra, ad 9 & 3 reduces, tunc 9 per 3 diuides, quotus erit 3, indicans 3/10 diuisorem in 9/10 diuidendo ter contineri. Atq; hic ut 3/10 ad 1 sunt, ita 9/10 ad 3, quare proin quotus diuisis partibus maior est.

Diuidantur 5/6 per 3/6, id est, quæratur, quoties 3/6 in 1/6 contineantur: hic primùm datas partes ad integra in ipsis proportionalia 5 & 3 reduces, tunc 5 per 3 diui-des, quotus erit 1 2/3. Vice versa, 3/6 per 5/6 diuisæ, quotum exhibent 3/5.

Sint porrò partes diuersi nominis diuidendæ, ut 3/4 per 1/3. Hic datas primùm partes cognominnes facies, sic, 9/12 & 4/12, tunc adhibita priore reductione ad integra, 9 per 4 diuides, quotus erit 2 1/4. Sint 8/9 per 5/6 diuidendæ: Partes igitur ad idem nomen, scilicet 16/18 & 15/18 rediges, tunc cognomines hasce partes ad integra 16 & 15 reduces, quæ inter se diuisa, quotum exhibent 1 1/15.

page.notes: Fractions are set as stacked numerators and denominators in the print; rendered here as simple fractions. The right-hand strip shows show-through and an adjoining page's text, not transcribed. Some fractional digits in the scan are doubtful (e.g. the denominators in the last paragraph) and are given as best read.
